business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K Item 1 business description
business_model.claim: Chatham is an internally managed REIT that owns hotels and earns its money from hotel operations, focused on upscale extended-stay and premium-branded select-service hotels.
quotes: The Company is internally-managed and invests primarily in upscale extended-stay and premium-branded select-service hotels.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K, the earnings release and the cash flow statement
business_model.claim: The portfolio grew from 33 hotels at the 2025 year-end to 39 hotels in the third-quarter 2026 release, mainly through a six-hotel Hilton-branded acquisition in March.
quotes: In March, Chatham acquired six Hilton-branded hotels comprising 589 rooms for $92 million.
The company owns 39 hotels totaling 5,610 rooms/suites in 18 states and the District of Columbia.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K Item 1 and Item 1A
business_model.claim: Because of REIT rules the company cannot operate its hotels. It leases each hotel to a taxable REIT subsidiary lessee, which hires third-party managers. Lease revenue between the company and its lessees is eliminated, so consolidated revenue is hotel revenue.
quotes: To maintain our qualification as a REIT, the Company cannot operate its hotels.
Lease revenue from each TRS Lessee is eliminated in consolidation.

Each hotel is leased to a TRS Lessee under a percentage lease that provides for rental payments equal to the greater of (i) a fixed base rent amount or (ii) a percentage rent based on hotel room revenue.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K, though as a description of the hotel category
business_model.claim: Customers are mainly business travelers, short-term transient guests and people on extended assignments or corporate relocations, who buy hotel rooms. The 10-K describes this customer base for extended-stay and all-suite hotels.
quotes: principal customer base includes business travelers, whether short-term transient travelers or those on extended assignments and corporate relocations;

business_model.claim: The company reports one segment, so there is no segment breakdown of revenue or profit.
quotes: We evaluate all of our hotels as a single industry segment because all of our hotels have similar economic characteristics and provide similar services to similar types of customers.

business_model.basis: stated in the income statement and MD&A
business_model.claim: Room rental is almost all of revenue. In the third quarter, room revenue was 83,339 of total revenue of 90,921 (table in thousands), and room revenue was 91.7% of total revenue. The rest is food and beverage (1,598), other hotel revenue such as parking and meeting rooms (5,686), and reimbursed costs from related parties (298).
quotes: Room revenue comprised 91.7% and 91.7% of total revenue for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-Q MD&A table and the earnings release
business_model.claim: The main revenue driver is RevPAR, the product of occupancy and average daily rate. In the third quarter same-property RevPAR rose 8.3% to $161.47 from $149.14, with occupancy of 83.0% versus 79.1% and ADR of $194.45 versus $188.58.
quotes: which is the product of occupancy and ADR, and does not include food and beverage revenue, or other operating revenue

business_model.claim: Third-quarter total revenue rose 16.0% to $90.9 million. The 10-Q attributes the increase to higher same-property RevPAR and the six hotels acquired in 2026, which added $7.2 million of third-quarter revenue.
quotes: The increase in total revenue primarily was related to the 8.3% increase in same property RevPAR and the acquisition of six hotels in 2026, which contributed $7.2 million of revenue during the three months ended September 30, 2026.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-Q MD&A and income statement
business_model.claim: Hotel operating costs are the largest cost line and move with the number of rooms sold, inflation and portfolio size. Third-quarter hotel operating expenses rose 13.8% to $50.1 million from $44.0 million, which the 10-Q attributes to the acquired hotels and inflation.
quotes: The increase in hotel operating expenses was related primarily to the acquisition of six hotels in 2026, which contributed $4.0 million in operating expenses during the three months ended September 30, 2026, and the impact of inflation.

business_model.basis: stated in the income statement and the 10-K; the link between fees and revenue is inferred from the base-fee definition
business_model.claim: A large part of hotel costs are payments to brand franchisors and the related-party manager. The manager is owned by the CEO and is paid a base fee as a percentage of the hotel's gross room revenue.
quotes: Base management fees are calculated as a percentage of the hotel's gross room revenue.
As of December 31, 2025, IHM managed all 33 of our hotels.

business_model.basis: stated in the earnings release; the operating-leverage mechanism is inferred from the margin and expense figures

quotes: Adjusted Hotel EBITDA margins rose 190 basis points to 39 percent in the 2026 third quarter.

business_model.basis: stated in the earnings release market table
business_model.claim: Results depend on location. Silicon Valley is the largest market at 18% of last-twelve-month Adjusted Hotel EBITDA, and its third-quarter RevPAR rose 23% to $174. Greater New York and Coastal Northeast RevPAR fell in the quarter.
quotes: Silicon Valley continues to be our hottest market and sets us apart from our peers moving forward.

business_model.claim: Revenue is seasonal, with the second and third quarters stronger. The third-quarter results are therefore a seasonally strong period.
quotes: Generally, we expect that we will have lower revenue, operating income and cash flow in the first and fourth quarters and higher revenue, operating income and cash flow in the second and third quarters.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-Q MD&A, the balance sheet and the 10-K risk factors
